# Focused code review

Ready with fixes. The branch has six findings, including one P1 approval-scope defect. A separate pre-existing finding does not affect the verdict.

Scope: `docs/ontology-reuse-baseline` at `f2615cab57cf7fe29ea27dfd01a476b3e7fd213e`, diffed against `main` at merge base `42ae9ac0e564e3eff7610cd8e975b6cc6f9c92a4`.

## Round-4 verification

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Purpose preserves section 11 status and gates only new imports | Pass at `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:4`. No old blanket-gate wording remains in the repository. Finding 1 concerns the remaining approval scope, not the removed blanket gate. |
| Section 1a says "These five" and has the five requested rows | Pass at line 13 and lines 17-21. Findings 4 and 7 concern other rows and summaries. |
| OM is plain text with a TLS-failure note | Pass at line 60. It is the only OM row in the repository. Its former HTTPS target fails certificate hostname validation. |
| No contradictions or stale wording | Fail. See findings 1-7. |
| Links resolve | Pass. `python3 scripts/check_doc_links.py` reports `OK: 55 relative doc links resolve.` All 25 unique external URLs in the new document also resolved. GS1 returned HTTP 403 to the generic command-line client but its EPCIS page was readable through the web fetcher. Link resolution does not validate the claims on those pages. |

## Findings

| # | Severity | Defect kind | Primary location | Route |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | P1 | Governance and approval-scope contradiction | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:4` | Manual, downstream resolver, verification required |
| 2 | P2 | Missing license and redistribution evidence | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:45` | Manual, downstream resolver, verification required |
| 3 | P2 | Unversioned maturity claim | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:47` | Gated auto, downstream resolver, verification required |
| 4 | P2 | Stale count and cross-document status contradiction | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:34` | Gated auto, downstream resolver |
| 5 | P2 | Pre-existing governance status contradiction | `docs/architecture/epm-ece-ppc-operating-model.md:43` | Manual, downstream resolver, pre-existing |
| 6 | P3 | Upstream guidance not carried into the decision checkpoint | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:44` | Gated auto, downstream resolver, verification required |
| 7 | P2 | Source maturity and link-target mismatch | `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:19` | Gated auto, downstream resolver |

### 1. One approval can authorize contradictory or non-import outcomes

**Evidence:** Line 4 proposes the import set "once" and makes approval a document-level event. Lines 25 and 34 repeat approval of "this proposal". Section 2 then mixes mutually exclusive choices, fallback options, an unresolved import-versus-shapes choice, and pattern-only reuse.

A reviewer can approve the document without determining which imports are actually approved. That can admit both BFO and GIST despite the instruction not to import both. It can also advance CCO before its fallback condition, select EPCIS import before its open design choice, or treat PREMIS as an import despite the explicit borrow-only instruction. The section 11 pointer repeats the same document-level gate.

Every affected location:

- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:4`, `:25`, and `:34`: set-level approval wording.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:36`: all section 2 rows sit under "Proposed to adopt with caveats".
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:42`: BFO and GIST are mutually exclusive.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:44`: CCO is conditional on BFO and GIST disappointing.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:46`: EPCIS import versus event-shape reuse remains undecided.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:47`: PREMIS is borrow-only, not an import candidate.
- `docs/architecture/shared-technical-foundation.md:120`: candidates become dependencies when the document's proposal is approved.

Separate import candidates from mutually exclusive choices, fallbacks, and pattern-only reuse. Record approval per row or per decision, with caveats resolved before dependency status changes.

Confidence: 100, from the independent adversarial reviewer. This P1 was found by one read and retains `requires_verification: true`.

### 2. SAREF's free download does not establish reuse rights

**Evidence:** Line 45 says "ETSI publishes the suite free and versioned" under "Proposed to adopt". [ETSI's IPR page](https://www.etsi.org/intellectual-property-rights) says ETSI owns the copyright with all rights reserved. It says reproduction may be allowed through a copyright-license request. Its separate software exception has limited purposes, and the baseline does not establish how that exception applies to the selected OWL artifacts. [SAREF4INMA](https://saref.etsi.org/saref4inma/) explicitly places its extracted specification under the ETSI IPR Policy.

The only affected repository row is `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:45`. Line 7's statement that licenses were read from the ETSI portal makes the missing permission conclusion material, but is not a second defective row.

Record the exact redistribution and derivative-work terms for the SAREF artifacts before import approval. Public availability alone does not establish those rights.

Confidence: 75, independent adversarial reviewer. Legal or license-owner verification remains necessary.

### 3. PREMIS is recommended without its draft-version status

**Evidence:** Line 47 says PREMIS was "Verified on the LoC page" but does not pin a version. [The Library of Congress page](https://www.loc.gov/standards/premis/ontology/) calls the revised ontology based on PREMIS 3 a draft. It separately identifies the earlier ontology based on PREMIS 2.2. Following the unversioned link can put draft v3 shapes into ECE's evidence model as though they were settled.

Every affected location:

- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:47`: unversioned PREMIS reuse recommendation.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:64`: unversioned PREMIS plus PROV-O is used to reject FaBiO and BIBO.

Pin the intended version. Label v3 as draft, or use the released 2.2 ontology when stability is required.

Confidence: 75, independent adversarial reviewer.

### 4. SKOS remains outside the existing-import summaries

**Evidence:** Line 13 correctly says "These five" and lines 17-21 include SKOS, PROV-O, OWL-Time, DCAT 3, and DCMI Terms. The Related paragraph and both approval summaries still reduce the existing set to four. The section 11 pointer also gates "candidates beyond" those four, which can put SKOS back under the new-proposal gate despite the Purpose preserving every section 11 entry's status.

Every affected location:

- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:5`: "those four" names only PROV-O, OWL-Time, DCAT, and DCMI Terms as concrete imports.
- `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:34`: "Section 11's four named vocabularies" omits SKOS.
- `docs/architecture/shared-technical-foundation.md:120`: "the four this table already names" omits SKOS and gates candidates beyond them.

Include all five existing entries in these statements. If SKOS is deliberately a format rather than a concrete import, state that distinction and remove the conflicting section 1a claim that all five are concrete imports.

Confidence: 100, found independently by the correctness read and the local adversarial reviewer. Agreement does not add cross-model promotion because both reads use the same serving family.

### 5. Pre-existing architecture text treats the open EPM import as settled

**Evidence:** `docs/charter.md:165-168` leaves the EPM import as open decision 3. The new baseline correctly preserves that status at line 79. Older architecture files describe the import as present fact, so an implementer can build against EPM before the owner decides.

Every affected location:

- `docs/architecture/epm-ece-ppc-operating-model.md:43`: "ECE imports rather than forks".
- `docs/architecture/shared-technical-foundation.md:25`: "imported Downstream Oil and Gas Ontology (from EPM)".
- `docs/architecture/solution-architecture.md:29`: "Retain EPM domain imports".
- `docs/architecture/solution-architecture.md:96`: "Domain meaning comes from versioned EPM imports".
- `docs/architecture/source/ece-solution-architecture.dot:31`: "EPM domain imports + ECE context".
- `docs/architecture/ece-solution-architecture.svg:180`: the same rendered assertion.

These lines predate the branch. The conditional wording in `docs/strategy/synthetic-data-generation-strategy.md:90` and `:356` is not defective because it explicitly preserves open decision 3.

Qualify each assertion as proposed or conditional until the decision is recorded. Update the DOT source and regenerate the SVG if those files change. This pre-existing finding is report-only for the branch verdict.

Confidence: 100, independent adversarial reviewer, with line-history evidence.

### 6. CCO reconsideration is set for 3.0 despite upstream guidance to wait for 4.0

**Evidence:** Line 44 proposes to "re-examine at CCO 3.0" after citing structural 3.0 and 4.0 changes. [The CCO governance board's README](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/CommonCoreOntology/CommonCoreOntologies/develop/README.md) recommends that users wait to update following the 4.0 release. The baseline does not explain why ECE should reconsider adoption during the earlier transition.

The only affected repository row is `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:44`. Its license, push date, and 2.2 release date matched the repository API.

Move the checkpoint to 4.0, or record why a 3.0 review is justified while keeping adoption conditional on a fresh stability review.

Confidence: 75, independent adversarial reviewer. This is a P3 decision-guidance defect, not a claim that CCO artifacts are unavailable.

### 7. The OWL-Time link contradicts the claimed Recommendation maturity

**Evidence:** Line 19 links the current OWL-Time technical report and calls it a 2017 W3C Recommendation. [The linked page](https://www.w3.org/TR/owl-time/) now identifies itself as a Candidate Recommendation Draft and says it is work in progress. [The dated 2017 page](https://www.w3.org/TR/2017/REC-owl-time-20171019/) does identify a W3C Recommendation.

The only affected repository row is `docs/architecture/ontology-reuse-baseline.md:19`. The defect is the undated link and missing current-draft qualification, not the existence of the 2017 Recommendation.

Link the dated 2017 Recommendation and note the current draft separately if it matters to the import decision.

Confidence: 100, correctness read.

## Actionable findings

Findings 1, 2, 3, 4, 6, and 7 belong to this branch. Findings 1, 2, 3, and 6 need the stated targeted verification after correction. Finding 5 is pre-existing and is excluded from the branch's apply queue and verdict.

## How this could pass review while still being wrong

A commit-scoped check can see the three requested edits at lines 4, 13, and 60 without reading the older summaries at lines 5 and 34 or the pointer at shared-technical-foundation line 120. A text assertion for "These five" does not prove consistent classification elsewhere.

The repository link checker tests only whether relative files exist. HTTP 200 responses likewise prove reachability, not reuse rights or maturity. SAREF's copyright terms, PREMIS's draft v3 status, and OWL-Time's current draft all survive a link-only review.

Non-binding wording also does not define approval granularity. One document approval can look valid while leaving BFO-versus-GIST, CCO's fallback, EPCIS's reuse form, and PREMIS's borrow-only status unresolved. Diff-only review misses the older EPM assertions in Markdown, DOT, and SVG.

## Coverage and limits

The focused path ran one correctness read and one independent local adversarial read. The cross-model pass did not run because the host serving family could not be attested. No other reviewer agents or separate validator ran.

No `AGENTS.md`, `REVIEW_STANDARDS.md`, `CODING_STANDARDS.md`, or `CLAUDE.md` governs the changed files. No review plan or declared Compound Pack applied. Repository occurrence searches were lexical over the current tree, including the editable DOT and generated SVG. Differently worded equivalents cannot be ruled out absolutely.

Selected GitHub license, activity, and release claims matched their primary sources. The review did not perform an exhaustive ontology survey or legal review. No ontology import, SHACL validation, or Neo4j/n10s RDF 1.2 round-trip was run, so runtime and semantic compatibility remain unproved.
